newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine bonds put in modest climb in quiet trade.
newsitem.headline: Argentine bonds put in modest climb in quiet trade.

text.p: Argentine bonds finished flat to higher Friday after another session spent closely watching U.S. Treasuries.

The market was kept afloat by the strong demand for bonds at Thursday's auction of 30-year Treasuries in the United States. Activity was modest, however, ahead of the Monday holiday in the United States.
Argentina's FRB due 2005 was flat at 83-3/4, while the local dollar-denominated Bocon Previsional 2 due 2001 rose $0.10 to 119.60.
An analyst said "the outlook is generally good with low international yield levels and attractive returns in Argentine bonds."

After a couple of weeks of profit-taking as investors booked some of the large gains they made this year the market rebounded at the end of last week and that turn was sustained in the last couple of sessions. Bond prices ended this week above their levels seven days ago.
But still traders have said for a couple of weeks now that investors have been staying on the sidelines as they close their portfolios for the year.
However, "I expect the market to recover the upside trend, at least to a level where the last correction began," said Roberto Costa Bourdieu, senior fixed income analyst at Banco Rio.
On Monday though, the market is set to be quiet due to the U.S. holiday.
In the money markets, call money rates fell to 6.83 percent from 6.93 percent.
